$comment: Byte-level fixed vectors for the Nowhere wire protocol, language-agnostic. Source: NodePassProject/Nowhere src/tests/protocol/*.rs (v1.8.2 @ 8807960c). The authentication section has additionally been recomputed by an independent implementation following docs/protocol.md section 2. All hex is lowercase and unseparated.

baseline.note: v1.8.2 released 2026-08-26. Advanced from v1.8.0 on the first normative change the drift check has reported: TLS Mux shard density 12 -> 4 flows, and a Portal-side QUIC memory-profile default. Both are runtime tuning; no wire field, layout, length, ordering or derivation moved, so every byte-level vector below carries across unchanged. Authentication and FlowHeader are additionally unchanged since 1.7. See conformance/PROTOCOL_BASELINE for the assessment.

notes: The shared key is strictly percent-decoded; a literal + stays +, it is not decoded as a space.
Tag comparison must be constant time.
Authentication has no response frame; a failure must not produce a distinguishable response (no active-probing oracle).
0xff cannot be a valid first FlowHeader byte (its role bits are the reserved value 0b11), which is why it is used as the TLS Mux mode marker.
For DUPLEX, up must equal down; for OPEN and ATTACH they must differ.

target.layout: atyp(u8) || address || port(u16 big-endian); ATYP values match SOCKS5

rejects.name: port 0
rejects.reason: port zero is invalid for every target form

notes: The domain is an unresolved ASCII/IDNA hostname; it must not include a port or IPv6 brackets.
Every rejection must happen before the target connection is attempted.
For a split flow only the selected downlink receives the result, and that result is authoritative for the whole logical flow.
The client must map all seven rejection reasons to distinct user-facing messages and log lines; they must not collapse into a generic connection failure.

rejects.name: EOF before the declared payload completes

notes: Consecutive packets are encoded back to back with no additional type field.
A clean EOF before the next length field closes that UoT half.

quicDatagram.typeBits: low two bits of the first byte; the remaining bits are reserved and must be zero

cases.name: FRAGMENT first fragment (2500-byte payload, maxDatagram 1200, 3 fragments)
never fragment when the whole packet fits

rejects.name: inconsistent fragment metadata for one packet (count / totalLen / flowId / packetId)
duplicate fragment with different bytes discards the whole packet
reassembled length not equal to totalLen discards the packet
DATA received before READY is discarded

notes: fragmentPayloadMax = maxDatagramSize - 13; fragmentCount = ceil(len / fragmentPayloadMax), and must fall in 2..255.
If the QUIC maximum datagram size shrinks and a packet must be replanned, the sender uses a new packetId; packetId allocation skips zero.
Reassembly is keyed by (flowId, packetId); upstream bounds it to 64 concurrent slots with a 10-second lifetime.

tlsMux.markerNote: Written after the AuthFrame; Portal does not echo it. Both directions then use Mux frames. Mux never wraps QUIC.

kinds.02: WINDOW (value = returned byte credit, flowId 0 means connection-level)

rejects.name: a DATAGRAM kind closes the Mux carrier as unsupported
RST must be the only flag and value must be 0
all other STREAM flag bits must be zero
WINDOW must have flags=0, no payload, and nonzero credit
credit exceeding the configured window closes the carrier
STREAM data for an unknown flowId is a carrier error

notes: The Mux flowId must match the flowId inside the logical stream's FlowHeader.
Late FIN and RST processing must be idempotent; a late stream-local WINDOW for an already closed stream is ignored.
Payload must obtain both stream credit and connection credit before entering the outbound queue.
Sharding is runtime placement and adds no wire fields.
